selected_evidence.requirement: node1 permits node3->node4 tcp/23 transit traffic and logs it
selected_evidence.summary: VyOS forward-filter rule 10 (accept, log enable) committed for tcp dst 10.100.20.13:23 src 10.100.20.12; nft ruleset shows it hooked into the forward chain with counters incrementing; kernel log shows '[ipv4-FWD-filter-10-A] ... SRC=10.100.20.12 DST=10.100.20.13 ... SPT=44483 DPT=23 SYN' recorded for the final test attempt.

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 refuses node3->node4 tcp/23 transit traffic and logs the refusal
selected_evidence.summary: OPNsense config.xml given a 'reject' rule for tcp 10.100.20.12->10.100.20.13:23; pfctl -sr confirms 'block return in log quick on vtnet0 ... proto tcp from 10.100.20.12 to 10.100.20.13 port = telnet'; pflog0 capture shows 'rule 75/0(match): block in on vtnet0: 10.100.20.12.44483 > 10.100.20.13.23: Flags [S]' for the same final attempt, with node2 sending the spoofed RST back to node3.

selected_evidence.requirement: Single attempt from node3 produces a correlated pair of log entries showing where traffic stopped
selected_evidence.summary: One nc connection attempt from node3 (exit=1, refused) at source port 44483 is recorded on node1 as accepted+logged (passed) and on node2 as blocked+logged (refused) for the identical 5-tuple, demonstrating the traffic reached node1, was forwarded, and was stopped at node2.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 2eb8b6e8...; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; boot_id changed to 0c94523f...; post-restart VyOS config (firewall rule 10, static route, send_redirects sysctls) confirmed persisted via 'show configuration commands'; post-restart forward-log entry (sport 33391) proves the permit+log path still functions.

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime 04:34:59; reboot acknowledged; kern.boottime changed to 04:40:45 proving genuine restart; post-restart pfctl -sr shows both the reject rule and the SSH management pass rule intact; post-restart pflog capture (sport 33391) shows the block+log rule still firing on the same attempt logged by node1.

selected_evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 8d2fbd8f...; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 15122ab7... with uptime 0 min; post-restart network/DHCP recovered (10.100.20.12/24 on eth0); node3 successfully re-ran the test connection attempt afterward, confirming full functional recovery.

selected_evidence.requirement: node4 restart: baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 41cf6b28...; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 851ca9d1... with uptime 0 min; post-restart network recovered with the same DHCP address 10.100.20.13/24, and the final end-to-end test (after all 4 nodes cycled) confirmed node4 remains the correct, reachable destination in the chain (traffic is correctly stopped upstream at node2 before reaching it).
